recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It completes the published actor-wording change in the authoritative current build source; no further core FHIR work is needed unless the work group wants a broader terminology cleanup of AuditEvent source labels.
issue_request: FHIR-32465 was Published as Not Persuasive with Modification for R5. It objected that AuditEvent source wording tied the event to a source system even though AuditEvent.source.observer can reference non-system resources such as Patient and RelatedPerson. The approved resolution was to use actor rather than system wording and explain that a human, such as a medical-records clerk recording a manual disclosure, may be the source for that audit record.
initial_application: Git commit 1a6b0f845f908e6df0334fec41da7a6543a863c0 changed the parent AuditEvent.source definition from system to actor and added the medical-records-clerk comment. It did not update AuditEvent.source.observer, which still described an identifier/source system before this reconciliation.
additional_context: AuditEvent is an active build resource in source/fhir.ini. FHIR-26377 previously kept human actors eligible as AuditEvent sources, FHIR-32461 expanded AuditEvent.source.observer target profiles to participant actor types, and Security WG block-vote evidence confirms FHIR-32465's disposition. No conflicting later source or community evidence was found.
reconciliation: Updated source/auditevent/structuredefinition-AuditEvent.xml so AuditEvent.source.observer is defined as a reference to the actor that detected and is reporting the event, and its requirements now tie the event to a reporting actor rather than to a specific source system.
source_changes: source/auditevent/structuredefinition-AuditEvent.xml: updated AuditEvent.source.observer definition and requirements from identifier/source-system wording to reporting-actor wording.
